text: I need to clarify the characteristics of your enlarged supraclavicular lymph node; is it hard, fixed, and non-tender, and do you have any history of smoking or recent dental infections? Additionally, have you experienced any recent fever spikes or loss of appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant weight loss and night sweats, I need to assess your abdominal pain more closely; is it located specifically in the right upper quadrant or epigastric area, and have you noticed any jaundice or changes in your bowel habits? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Liver Function Tests, and ESR.

speaker: Doctor
text: With your blood work being normal, I need to focus on the abdominal pain and lymph node characteristics; is your pain sharp or dull, and does pressing on the supraclavicular area cause it to become tender or fixed? Additionally, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or a sensation of food getting stuck? REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with contrast.

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma. The combination of supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, massive involvement of axillary and mediastinal nodes on CT, and systemic B-symptoms (night sweats, weight loss, fatigue) is highly suggestive of a lymphoproliferative disorder.
